To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neuromodulatory current IMI, which is activated by a G-proteins-coupled Ca2+-sensing receptor, is regulated by calmodulin and CaMKII.
the voltage dependence and Ca2+ sensitivity of the neuromodulator-activated inward current IMI is regulated by the GPCR family calcium sensing receptor CaSR.

the neuromodulatory current (IMI), which is an inward current generated by the stomatogastrics neurons of the crab Cancer borealis, loses its voltage dependence when extracellular Ca2+ concentration is low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the voltage dependence of a calcium-sensitive neuromodulator current, which has been shown to play a role as a pacemaker current for a central pattern generator in the crab stomatogastrical ganglion.
a novel mechanism of voltage dependence in which extracellular calcium is sensed by a CaSR, which in turn regulates IMI voltage dependence via intracellular signaling pathways.
the voltage dependence of an important neuromodulatory current, IMI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the voltage dependence is regulated by a CaSR, which is activated by extracellular Ca2+ and is coupled to the G-protein Gβγ, and that this signaling pathway activates a CaMKII-mediated phosphorylation of IMI, which is necessary for IMI voltage-dependence.
the voltage dependence is mediated by the G-protein-couple CaSR, which acts downstream of calmodulin and CaMKII.
the voltage dependence in IMI is regulated by a CaSR and that this is mediated by the Gαi/o subunits, the myosin light-chain kinase pathway, and the Gβγ pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the voltage dependence is regulated by a CaSR that is activated in conditions of high extracellular calcium and that the CaSR is regulated by intracellular CaMKII and G-protein-couple receptors.
the voltage dependence for a neuromodulatory current is regulated by a Ca2+-sensing receptor and that this regulation is mediated by Gβγ and myosin light-chain kinase.

the voltage dependence for a neuromodulatory ionic current can be regulated by a CaSR and that the regulation of this voltage dependence may play a role in the regulation of the pyloric rhythm of the stomatogastrica system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the voltage dependence and therefore the oscillatory activity of a neuromodulated ionic current is regulated by an intracellular signaling pathway, in this case a Ca2+-dependent G-protein-couple receptor.
IMI voltage dependence appears to be regulated through an intracellular pathway activated by extracellular Ca2+.
the voltage dependence in IMI is not due to a direct interaction with calmodulin, but rather is due to a CaSR-mediated pathway.
